title: Christians (Acts 11:19–26)
hookLine: in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians
last: SHE WAS FULL OF GOOD WORKS.

cards: For the first years after Jesus, his followers had no one name. In Acts they're the disciples, the brethren, the saints, the believers, and people of the Way.
Then, in a big, noisy, mixed city in Syria, somebody gave them a name. The text doesn't say who. And the name stuck.
It started in a single city, at a single moment, and Luke wrote the moment down.

teach.b: The city is Antioch, a great city of Roman Syria. After Stephen's death, believers scattered and spoke the word only to fellow Jews.
But some men from Cyprus and Cyrene came to Antioch and spoke to Greeks as well, and a great number believed.

Jerusalem sends Barnabas, the son of encouragement. He sees what's happening, and the text says he was glad. Then he does something wise: he goes to Tarsus to find Saul, the new convert from Damascus, and brings him back.
The two of them teach in Antioch for a whole year. Then the line, in the Douay-Rheims: "at Antioch the disciples were first named Christians." In Greek, Christianoi.
The ending is a Latin-style one, used for a party or a household: Caesar's people, Herod's people. So the name likely meant Christ's people, the Messiah's crowd.

Some readers think outsiders coined it, maybe half as a joke. The word turns up again from King Agrippa's lips later in Acts, and in First Peter, where believers are told not to be ashamed if they suffer as one.
So a name perhaps given by neighbors became a name people were willing to die for.

Antioch has another place in Catholic memory. Tradition says Peter led the church there before Rome. And a later bishop of Antioch, Ignatius, wrote a letter that calls the Church catholic, meaning universal.

how: Catholics receive their Christian name at baptism, often a saint's name, and the Church keeps the feast of the Chair of Saint Peter on February 22, which once had a separate celebration for Peter's chair at Antioch.

games.q: you're Barnabas. the church in Antioch is growing fast, Jews and Greeks together, and it needs teaching. what do you do?
o: go to Tarsus and bring back Saul.
send to Jerusalem for the twelve.
games.why: he goes looking for Saul, the convert some still feared, and they teach together for a whole year.

practice: Sit for a moment with a name you carry, by faith or family or job.

If you are a Christian, notice that the word may first have come from neighbors who watched how believers lived; if the name isn't yours, think of one you do carry, a family name, a team, a title, and what it asks of you.
No grading, just noticing, and if you pray, ask to live up to your name.

wordCard.voice: Christian. Christ's people, the Messiah's people, a name first heard in Antioch and perhaps given by outsiders. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: Christian, one of Christ's people. Christos means anointed.
